SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 45.211944, -67.266111 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 105 gallon
Report Description/// UPDATE TO INCIDENT REPORT # 1384511 /// /// NEEC INCIDENT NOTIFICATION /// UPDATE: RECEIVED ON 2023-11-16 22:03 ET | CALLER REPORTS THAT A SUNBURY TRACTOR-TRAILER FELL OFF THE BRIDGE (THE CAUSE IS UNKNOWN), DOWN 1600 FEET, ENDING UP 45 DEGREES ON THE EMBANKMENT, HANGING OVER DENNIS STREAM, WITH THE RADIATOR IN THE STREAM. BOTH SADDLE TANKS OF THE TRUCK ARE COMPLETELY EMPTY, DICTATING THAT 350 L – 400 L OF DIESEL HAS SPILLED UNTO THE EMBANKMENT AND VERY LIKELY INTO THE STREAM. CALLER EXPLAINS THAT THE EMBANKMENT IS CONSTRUCTED WITH SHALE ROCK (LARGE AND LOOSE ROCKS USED TO BUILD HIGHWAYS), AND THERE IS NO MORE DIESEL ODOR AT THE SITE OF THE ACCIDENT. SEEING IT IS DARK OUTSIDE, THE SPILL IS NOT VISIBLE, BUT IT IS VERY LIKELY THAT THE DIESEL SPILLED INTO THE STREAM. THE TRUCK WAS CARRYING CORRUGATED CARDBOARD. CALLER INDICATES THAT THE CALL WAS RECEIVED ON 2023-11-16 AT 19:51. ACCORDING TO SUNBURY, THE TRUCK’S COMPUTER TRACKING SYSTEM INDICATES THAT THE TRUCK CAME TO A STOP ON 2023-11-16 AT 18H58. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT CAME AND PINCHED THE FUEL LINE, AND SOME ABSORBENT PADS ARE BEING PLACED. BOTH THE FIRE DEPARTMENT AND THE POLICE HAVE LEFT. A RIVER BOOM WILL BE BROUGHT IN TO CATCH ANY REMNANT DIESEL. AT THIS POINT, IT IS UNKNOWN WHERE THE DIESEL HAS SPILLED. RST EMERGENCY RESPONSE AND THE INSURANCE ARE ON SITE. CALLER EXPLAINS THAT RST EMERGENCY RESPONSE IS A HAZMAT RESPONSE TEAM FROM TRANSPORT CANADA AND IS A SISTER COMPANY TO SUNBURY. BOTH COMPANIES ARE UNDER THE UMBRELLA OF IRVING OIL.

CALLER EXPLAINS THAT THE EMBANKMENT IS CONSTRUCTED WITH SHALE ROCK (LARGE AND LOOSE ROCKS USED TO BUILD HIGHWAYS), AND THERE IS NO MORE DIESEL ODOR AT THE SITE OF THE ACCIDENT. SEEING IT IS DARK OUTSIDE, THE SPILL IS NOT VISIBLE, BUT IT IS VERY LIKELY THAT THE DIESEL SPILLED INTO THE STREAM. THE TRUCK WAS CARRYING CORRUGATED CARDBOARD. CALLER INDICATES THAT THE CALL WAS RECEIVED ON 2023-11-16 AT 19:51. ACCORDING TO SUNBURY, THE TRUCK’S COMPUTER TRACKING SYSTEM INDICATES THAT THE TRUCK CAME TO A STOP ON 2023-11-16 AT 18H58. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT CAME AND PINCHED THE FUEL LINE, AND SOME ABSORBENT PADS ARE BEING PLACED. BOTH THE FIRE DEPARTMENT AND THE POLICE HAVE LEFT. A RIVER BOOM WILL BE BROUGHT IN TO CATCH ANY REMNANT DIESEL. AT THIS POINT, IT IS UNKNOWN WHERE THE DIESEL HAS SPILLED. RST EMERGENCY RESPONSE AND THE INSURANCE ARE ON SITE. CALLER EXPLAINS THAT RST EMERGENCY RESPONSE IS A HAZMAT RESPONSE TEAM FROM TRANSPORT CANADA AND IS A SISTER COMPANY TO SUNBURY. BOTH COMPANIES ARE UNDER THE UMBRELLA OF IRVING OIL.

Report DescriptionAMPLIFYING INFORMATION: - USCG SECTOR NORTHER NEW ENGLAND RECEIVED A NOTIFICATION FROM SEA TOW THAT THE MAINE MARITIME MUSEUM SAILING VESSEL (S/V) MARY E WITH 15 PASSENGERS AND 3 CREW MEMBERS WAS SINKING IN THE KENNEBEK RIVER NEAR DOUBLING POINT. - THE VESSEL WAS KNOCKED DOWN BIG A LARGE GUST OF WIND, CAPSIZED AND WAS UNABLE TO RIGHT ITSELF. - SECTOR NORTHER NEW ENGLAND ISSUED AN UMIB, LAUNCHED STATION BOOTHBAY HARBOR AND REQUESTED AIR SUPPORT FROM AIR STATION CAPE COD. - PRIOR TO CG ASSETS ARRIVING, SEA TOW AND BATH COUNTY FIRE RESPONDED, ARRIVED ON SCENE AND RESCUED AND ACCOUNTED FOR ALL 15 PASSENGERS AND 3 CREW MEMBERS. - 2 PASSENGERS RECEIVED EMS TREATMENT AND WERE TRANSFERRED TO MIDCOAST HOSPITAL: 1 ELDERLY FEMALE FOR POSSIBLE FRACTURES AND 1 ELDERLY MALE FOR HYPOTHERMIA. - MARINE PATROL UNITS ARE ON SCENE AND THE VESSEL HAS BEEN REPORTED AS A COMPLETE LOSS. - SECTOR NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND INVESTIGATIVE OFFICERS AND MARINE INSPECTORS HAVE BEEN NOTIFIED AND AND RESPONDING TO INVESTIGATE AND QUERY THE CREW AND PASSENGERS - THE VESSEL SANK WITH THE STERN AND STARBOARD QUARTER STICKING UP. - SECTOR NORTHER NEW ENGLAND ISSUED A SAFETY MARINE INFORMATION BROADCAST AND ESTABLISHED A SAFETY ZONE. - THERE CURRENTLY NO SIGNIFICANT MEDIA ATTENTION. - THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN.

CALLER EXPRESSES CONCERN BECAUSE THIS IS STILL CAUSING HEAVY FUMES THAT ARE HAVING HEALTH IMPACTS ON YOUNG CHILDREN. CALLER WANTS TO ENSURE CLEAN-UP IS COMPLETED. ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION FOR NRC REPORT 1332574: UNKNOWN SHEEN SIGHTING. EXACT SOURCE OF THE SHEEN IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME. CALLER STATES THE FIRE DEPT IS ONSCENE AND THEY SUSPECT THE SHEEN COULD HAVE ORIGINATED FROM A BURNED DOWN RESTAURANT AT THE ADDRESS LOCATION. CALLER WAS TOLD THE AMOUNT OF FUEL IN THE WATER COULD POSSIBLY BE 100 GALLONS.
